title: The history and development of bicycle
titleCn: 自行车的历史与发展：安全自行车与社会影响

paragraphs.text: Part three.

You will hear two design and technology students called Max and Izzy planning their presentation about the history and development of the bicycle. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Hi, Izzy. Can we talk about our presentation?
Sure.
So our topic, the bicycle, its history and its effect on society in the Western world. We should start with its invention in the eighteen hundreds.
The first bike wasn't very successful, was it? I think the model they call the safety bicycle is more significant.
Yes. Was that named because it was safe for cyclists of all ages, including young kids?

I think it was more to do with the comparison to previous versions, which got their speed from one large wheel. This bike had equally sized wheels and its speed came from gears. It was an important development as it was the first model that actually looked like a bike you'd see today.
Right. And the development of that bicycle at the end of the nineteenth century had an enormous impact on the working classes.
You mean how it gave them freedom to move around and look for jobs?
I suppose before the bike, they didn't have private transport, so were limited in where they could work.

Right. Because it took such a long time to go anywhere. But I'd really like to draw attention to how inhabitants of rural areas were able to travel outside their communities, and that led them to marrying people they never could have met in the past. That changed society, and I'd like to discuss it in our presentation.
Oh, good idea.
So what should we stress about changing attitudes to bicycles in the twentieth century?

Well, the bicycle was an important means of transport through the early nineteen hundreds, and that continued until the nineteen fifties, when cars became available to the general population and much more popular. That led to people losing interest in bikes for a while.
I hadn't realized the impact that people's love of motorized transport had on the bike's reputation.
Yes, that's a key point we should make.
Then the fold-up bike and others came along in the sixties, which helped sales pick up.
Hmm. Then things stayed fairly stable until the fitness craze of the eighties peaked interest in mountain biking and sales went up. But the bike had lost its position as a key mode of transport.
Right.
I'd like to talk about some current projects around the world involving bikes.
How about the scheme in an American school that provides bikes for all its pupils? I expect the pupils are delighted, not to mention the parents.
I suppose so. Although I wonder how much it costs.
Probably not as much as other initiatives. I just wonder if the advantages really justify the scheme.
Well, it must enable pupils to get to school more easily.
But does attendance actually improve? If there's any data to support that, we need to include it, but I haven't found enough.
Let's look into that later.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.
Could we look at the results of the survey we did with cyclists? We each spoke to different people.

Yes. One of my first interviewees was David. He works from home and spends a lot of time indoors, so at weekends he goes out with a cycling club. He said it's a way to connect with people apart from the other benefits.
Okay. Who else?

Uh, I interviewed a woman called Marlene. I asked her what her main reason for using a bike was. She's got young children and doesn't have much free time, so cycling to work is a way for her to keep fit. That's what she liked about it.
Okay. How about Annabelle? Was she the one who sold her car and uses a bike instead? Was that because of pollution?
She did sell her car, but her choice to travel by bike was made for financial reasons, as she was paying so much for petrol.
I see. And Rashid, he was probably the oldest person we spoke to.

He's in his seventies, yes, and he's been cycling around the city for years. He said that there are several advantages, but he really loves the way it helps him think clearly and takes his mind off any worries he has.
Great.
What about you? Have you got notes about Saira?
Yes. I spoke to her last week. She lives in the countryside, and she loves being on her bike in the open air and enjoying the beautiful environment and landscape around her.
Right.

The last person I interviewed was Giovanni. He's very practical, and he said it's just easier for him to use a bike to get around town than to drive. He finds sitting in traffic and looking for parking spaces too time-consuming, so he switched to using a bike instead.
Great. Shall we meet next week? And then we can...
That is the end of part three. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to Part three.
